newsitem.title: UK: U.S. and Canadian bonds lead pack higher - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. and Canadian bonds lead pack higher - Salomon.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries led the Salomon world government bond index (WGBI) higher in the latest week, while Canadian bonds outstripped their counterparts over the month, according to data from Salomon Brothers.
The WGBI rose 0.54 percent during the last week of October in local currency terms, and was also up 1.68 percent during the whole month.

U.S. Treasuries, gaining 1.08 percent in the week, were cheered after economic data suggested inflationary pressures remained in check. The data reduced the likelihood of an imminent rise in U.S. interest rates.
Canadian bonds were in second position in the latest week, and in first place over the month with rises of 0.69 percent and 4.23 percent respectively in local terms.

The Bank of Canada cut its key bank rate by a total of 75 basis points to 3.50 percent in October, its lowest level since August 1963. This lowered its target range for the overnight lending rate to 3.0-3.50 percent from 3.25-3.75 percent.
Other strong performers in the week were Japan, with a local currency gain of 0.65 percent, and Italy which gained 0.22 percent.
Germany and France gained a mediocre 0.14 percent and 0.18 percent respectively, while British gilts lost 0.01 percent in the week.
The worst performers on a weekly basis were the Nordic countries, where Finland lost 0.38 percent and Sweden dipped 0.36 percent.
On the monthly index, the U.S. was beaten into second place in local terms, gaining 2.18 percent. Australian bonds were up 2.09 percent.
High-yielder Italy provided a 2.08 percent return, while Spain was up 1.35 percent and Sweden 1.08 percent, in local terms.
French bonds increased 1.24 percent on the month, while German Bunds gained 0.71 percent. Japan made a strong showing in the month, gaining 1.78 percent.

In dollar terms, the weekly winner was British gilts, providing a return of 2.31 percent, and beating Treasuries' 1.08 percent gain. The biggest loser in the week in dollar terms was Japan, which dropped 0.11 percent. Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
